summary: When outdoor AQI exceeds 300 (Very Poor / Severe), cloth and surgical masks leak most PM2.5 particles. Wear a well-fitted N95, KN95, or FFP2 respirator without an exhalation valve during essential outdoor trips. Keep children and elders indoors whenever possible.
citation: WHO & Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Air Pollution Guidance

summary: During winter mornings and nights, cold air traps pollutants under a shallow planetary boundary layer (<300m) with low wind (<6 km/h). Keep windows closed and place rolled damp cloths at door gaps during peaks (₹0). Open windows for 15–20 minutes in mid-afternoon when sunlight raises the boundary layer and AQI dips.
citation: CPCB Winter Smog Dispersion Advisory & SAFAR India

topic: DIY Corsi-Rosenthal Air Filter Box (5 Steps)
summary: A DIY Corsi-Rosenthal Box delivers 450–600 m³/h CADR for ₹2,200–₹3,500: (1) Gather 4 MERV-13 or replacement HEPA filters + 1 standard 40cm box fan + duct tape + cardboard base. (2) Tape the 4 filters into an open cube with arrows pointing inward. (3) Seal the cardboard base to the bottom. (4) Tape the box fan on top blowing UPWARD. (5) Cut a circular shroud ring on top to boost airflow by ~20%.
citation: UC Davis Engineering & UL Chemical Insights CADR Validation (2023)

summary: AVOID ozone-generating air purifiers and high-output ionizers: ground-level ozone irritates airways and worsens asthma. Use mechanical HEPA H13 or MERV-13 filtration only. Also, while indoor plants improve well-being, studies show you would need 100+ plants per m² to match one small HEPA filter for PM2.5.
citation: US EPA Guide to Air Cleaners in the Home & Drexel University Plant Study

summary: High-heat frying and tadka can spike indoor PM2.5 above 300 µg/m³. Cover pans with lids, run kitchen exhaust fans while cooking and 10 minutes after, avoid incense sticks and mosquito coils during smog days, and wet-mop floors instead of dry sweeping to keep settled dust out of the air.
citation: WHO Household Fuel Combustion & Indoor PM2.5 Guidance

topic: Zero Waste, Leaf, or Coal Burning
summary: Never burn dry leaves, garbage, wood, or charcoal braziers (angithi) indoors or in neighborhoods. Burning 1 kg of dry waste emits up to 18 g of toxic PM2.5 and carbon monoxide. Compost leaves, report municipal open burning under CPCB GRAP, and use warm layered clothing (₹0) or electric heaters instead.
citation: CPCB Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) & National Clean Air Programme

summary: AirNest does not diagnose medical conditions. If you or a family member experience severe shortness of breath, chest pain or tightness, bluish lips/nails, dizziness, or asthma symptoms that do not improve after using a prescribed reliever inhaler, call emergency medical services (112 / 108 in India) or visit the nearest emergency clinic immediately.
